description: Bug 1: money double-counted when two invariants fire on one order. In src/lib/runner/run.ts the per-journey moneyAtRiskMinor is [...violations, ...escalations].reduce((s,v)=>s+v.moneyAtRiskMinor,0). When two invariants object to the SAME order (one payable order == one intentId), that order's money is added once per rule. Proven: reg-04-expired-quote total ₹2798.00 = INV-INVENTORY ₹1399 + INV-QUOTE-EXPIRY ₹1399, but it is ONE ₹1399 order; same on pert-01 (₹2094 = 2×₹1047). Attribute money once per distinct order (intentId), not once per violation. This flows through to the suite-level moneyPreventedMinor / moneyNotPreventedMinor split (they aggregate the per-journey figure), so fixing the per-journey figure fixes both. HamperHub frozen numbers (8/10/2/5 -> 11/13/1/0, 12/12) must NOT change: the outcome counts and rules-exercised do not depend on the money total, but VERIFY demo:preflight after. The money-at-risk figure WILL change (it is currently inflated) and that is the intended correction.
steps: Read src/lib/runner/run.ts around the per-journey moneyAtRiskMinor computation (~line 631: `moneyAtRiskMinor: [...violations, ...escalations].reduce((sum, v) => sum + v.moneyAtRiskMinor, 0)`). Also read the identical audit-log money_at_risk computation (~line 545 in the run.completed audit.append output) which uses the same reduce and must be deduped the same way for consistency.
Read src/lib/policy/violations.ts to confirm Violation carries intentId (and quoteId) and moneyAtRiskMinor.

Implement a helper (near the runner, e.g. `sumMoneyAtRiskByOrder(rows)`) that dedups money by distinct order: group violations+escalations by intentId (fall back to quoteId, then to the content-derived id when intentId is null, so a violation with no intent still contributes once). Within a group, take the single per-order amount rather than summing duplicates — use the MAX moneyAtRiskMinor in the group (multiple rules objecting to one order all reference the same order value; max is the robust choice if they ever differ). Document WHY in a comment: one payable order is one intentId; two rules objecting to it is still one order's money at risk.
Apply the helper to the per-journey moneyAtRiskMinor field AND to the audit-log money_at_risk (toMajor(...)) computation so the audit trail and the journey agree.

Confirm the suite-level moneyPreventedMinor / moneyNotPreventedMinor / moneyAtRiskMinor (~line 880) still aggregate journeys.reduce over the now-deduped per-journey figure — no change needed there, but confirm prevented + not-prevented still == total.

Add a test in tests/honest-reporting.test.ts (or a focused new tests/money-dedup.test.ts following the same runSuite pattern): build/run a journey where two invariants fire on ONE order (reg-04-expired-quote is the canonical case — run REGRESSION_SCENARIOS or a synthetic two-invariant-one-order Scenario) and assert the journey's moneyAtRiskMinor equals the single order's money (e.g. 139900) NOT the doubled figure (279800). Also assert suite.moneyPreventedMinor + suite.moneyNotPreventedMinor === suite.moneyAtRiskMinor still holds.
Prove the test bites: temporarily revert the dedup (back to the summing reduce), run the new test, show it FAILS; restore the fix, show it PASSES. Record this evidence in findings.
Run npm run typecheck and npm test; confirm green.

Run LLM_ADAPTER=scripted PAYMENT_ADAPTER=fake npm run demo:preflight and confirm 8/10/2/5 -> 11/13/1/0 with 12/12 both UNCHANGED. Record the new (corrected, lower) money-at-risk figure and confirm reg-04 now shows ₹1399 not ₹2798 in the detail rows.
acceptance_criteria: Per-journey moneyAtRiskMinor attributes each order's money once (reg-04 = one ₹1399 order, not ₹2798)
New test fails when the dedup is reverted and passes when restored (evidence recorded)
demo:preflight outcome counts 8/10/2/5 -> 11/13/1/0 and 12/12 rules exercised UNCHANGED; money-at-risk figure corrected downward
findings:
IMPLEMENTED. Added sumMoneyAtRiskByOrder(rows) helper in src/lib/runner/run.ts (just after the perturbation import). It groups violations+escalations by intentId (fallback quoteId, then content-derived violation id when intentId is null so an intent-less violation still contributes once) and takes the MAX moneyAtRiskMinor per group rather than summing — one payable order is one intentId, so two rules objecting to it is still one order's money. Applied to BOTH the per-journey moneyAtRiskMinor field (~line 657) AND the run.completed audit-log money_at_risk toMajor(...) computation (~line 554) so audit and journey agree. Suite-level aggregation (~line 880) is unchanged; it sums the now-deduped per-journey figure and prevented+not-prevented==total still holds.

TEST: added describe 'money at risk is attributed once per order, not once per rule' in tests/honest-reporting.test.ts with two cases: (1) runs REGRESSION_SCENARIOS vulnerable, finds reg-04-expired-quote, asserts firedInvariants.length>1 AND journey.moneyAtRiskMinor === 139900 (one ₹1399 order, not doubled 279800); (2) asserts moneyPreventedMinor+moneyNotPreventedMinor === moneyAtRiskMinor for both vulnerable and fixed mutation sets.

REVERT-FAILS / RESTORE-PASSES EVIDENCE: temporarily reverted the per-journey field back to the summing reduce [...violations,...escalations].reduce((s,v)=>s+v.moneyAtRiskMinor,0) and ran the new test -> FAILED with 'AssertionError: expected 279800 to be 139900' (reg-04 = doubled ₹2798). Restored sumMoneyAtRiskByOrder -> test PASSED (2 passed / 14 skipped). Confirmed the test bites.

VERIFICATION: `npm run typecheck` clean. `npm test` green: 580 passed / 4 skipped (was 578/4; +2 new tests). `LLM_ADAPTER=scripted PAYMENT_ADAPTER=fake npm run demo:preflight` outcome counts UNCHANGED: vulnerable 8 passed / 10 safely-rejected / 2 escalated / 5 unsafe / 0 escapes -> fixed 11 / 13 / 1 / 0 / 0, 12/12 policy rules exercised in both, recall 8/8. Money-at-risk corrected DOWNWARD as intended: demo:preflight now ₹13,401.72 -> ₹9,809.00 (was inflated). The reg-04 detail row now shows ₹1399 with NO ₹2798 appearing anywhere in the output; reg-05-duplicate-payment shows the single ₹1,399.00.

SIDE EFFECT: tests/claims.test.ts pins published README money figures; updated the two atRisk expectations and the two README.contains assertions from ₹16,224.18/₹12,607.00 to the corrected ₹13,401.72/₹9,809.00, and updated the matching README.md 'Money at risk (prevented)' table row. Outcome counts / readiness / escapes in that test are unchanged.
